title: A Novel Weighted Loss TabTransformer Integrating Explainable AI for Imbalanced Credit Risk Datasets
authors: Hartomo, K.; Arthur, C.; Nataliani, Y.
tldr: A weighted loss TabTransformer with SHAP-based explainability improves credit risk classification on imbalanced datasets, raising BISAID accuracy from 86.35% to 89.27% and German Credit from 93% to 95%.
problem_and_motivation: Credit risk assessment suffers from class imbalance where defaults are underrepresented, causing biased predictions toward the majority class. Traditional ML models are opaque black boxes that erode trust among stakeholders. Financial institutions lack interpretable tools to explain credit decisions to borrowers, particularly for MSMEs where information asymmetry is prevalent.
approach: Proposed a TabTransformer model enhanced with weighted cross-entropy loss to address class imbalance in credit risk datasets.
Applied the framework to two datasets: BISAID (2563 Indonesian MSME records) and German Credit (1000 instances from UCI).
Computed class weights inversely proportional to class frequency, assigning higher penalties to minority classes during training.
Integrated SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) for post-modeling interpretability, identifying key predictors like Financing Needs and Credit Amount.
Conducted hyperparameter tuning with 10-fold cross-validation, optimizing dim, depth, heads, and dropout parameters.
findings: num: Weighted loss improved BISAID accuracy from 86.35% to 89.27%, with minority class AUC increasing from 0.88 to 0.91.
num: German Credit accuracy improved from 93% to 95%, with minority class precision rising from 0.85 to 0.88 and recall from 0.93 to 0.97.
SHAP analysis identified Financing Needs (average SHAP value 0.65) as the most significant predictor in BISAID, and Credit Amount (0.12) in German Credit.
Weighted loss smoothed training and validation loss curves, reducing overfitting tendency observed in non-weighted training.
Minority classes (classes 2 and 3 in BISAID) showed notable AUC improvement from 0.88/0.86 to 0.91/0.91 respectively.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper proposes a novel framework combining TabTransformer with weighted cross-entropy loss to address class imbalance in credit risk classification. It demonstrates that weighted loss significantly improves minority class performance without degrading majority class accuracy. The integration of SHAP provides transparent feature attribution, identifying Financing Needs and Credit Amount as key predictors. The framework establishes a reliable, equitable, and transparent approach to credit evaluation that balances predictive accuracy with interpretability for financial institutions and borrowers.
directly_justifies: Weighted loss improves minority class AUC from 0.88 to 0.91 on BISAID and overall accuracy from 86.35% to 89.27%.
German Credit minority class precision and recall rose from 0.85/0.93 to 0.88/0.97 with weighted loss.
SHAP identifies Financing Needs (average SHAP 0.65) as the most significant predictor in BISAID dataset.
Weighted loss smooths training curves and reduces overfitting tendency compared to non-weighted training.
limits: Limited to two datasets (BISAID and German Credit) which may not represent all credit risk scenarios.
Does not compare against other imbalanced learning techniques like SMOTE or cost-sensitive learning beyond weighted loss.
The TabTransformer hyperparameters were manually tuned rather than using automated optimization methods.
No real-time deployment or integration with existing financial institution systems was demonstrated.
